classification.difficultyReason: Count five-digit palindromes using independent digit choices, then express their number as a percentage of all five-digit numbers.

content.prompt: The number $12\,321$ is a palindrome since it is unchanged when its digits are reversed. What percentage of five-digit numbers are palindromes?

answer.short:
$1\%$

A five-digit palindrome is determined by its first three digits; its last two digits mirror the first two.
answer.worked:
A five-digit palindrome has the form $abcba$. There are 9 choices for $a$ (1–9), 10 choices for $b$ and 10 choices for $c$. The last two digits are then fixed.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Number of palindromes}&=9\times10\times10\\\text{Number of palindromes}&=900\end{align*}$$

For all five-digit numbers, the first digit has 9 choices and each remaining digit has 10 choices.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Number of five-digit numbers}&=9\times10\times10\times10\times10\\\text{Number of five-digit numbers}&=90\,000\\\text{Percentage that are palindromes}&=\frac{900}{90\,000}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage that are palindromes}&=1\%\end{align*}$$
